newsitem.title: FRANCE: C.A.R. nationals occupy Bangui Paris embassy.
newsitem.headline: C.A.R. nationals occupy Bangui Paris embassy.

text.p: A small group of nationals of the Central African Republic said on Monday they had taken over their country's embassy in Paris to protest against French military intervention in Bangui.

"There are about a dozen of us in the embassy and more are coming," said Henri Grothe, who answered the embassy's telephone, identifying himself as spokesman for the "Action Committee for Peace in Central Africa."
Grothe said there were four embassy personnel inside the building but they were free to leave when they wanted.
"There was no violence and we are not holding hostages," said Grothe whose group carried out a peaceful daylong occupation of the embassy a month ago for the same reasons.

The group demanded that France withdraw its forces from Bangui where there was a weekend of bloody clashes between army mutineers and French forces, who launched helicopter-led raids to avenge the killing of two French officers.
